title: Olfactory display for XR
bottleneck: Smell is tightly linked to memory and emotion, but no practical scent display exists for XR: chemical cartridges are bulky, scents linger and contaminate, switching between odors takes seconds to minutes, and synthesizing arbitrary smells from primaries is unsolved chemistry. Digital scent remains a perennial demo that never ships.
why_it_blocks: Without smell, virtual environments miss a dimension that strongly drives presence and memory; training simulations (firefighting, medicine, cooking) lose critical cues. The chemical nature of olfaction resists digitization.
current_state: Scent cartridges exist for niche VR and marketing installations with a handful of preloaded odors. General-purpose, fast-switching, compact olfactory displays are still research prototypes. Scent molecules linger in air and on surfaces, so rapid context switching between smells is physically impossible with chemical delivery.
